Published online:
September 3, 2026

Geographic focus:
Germany (Europe)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — references Q2 2026 GDP outturn and prior Ifo summer forecasts
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — near-term fiscal stimulus and energy price drag on household consumption
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — GDP, inflation and energy price outlook through 2028

Synopsis:
Ifo raised its German GDP growth forecasts to 1.4% (2026) and 1.2% (2027), driven by fiscal stimulus (~€40bn, 0.8% of GDP) in infrastructure, defence and climate, alongside stronger industrial output and export demand. A better-than-expected Q2 2026 (+0.3%) also contributed to the upgrade. The key downside risk is persistently elevated energy prices tied to the Iran war, which suppresses household consumption and keeps inflation elevated (2.8% in 2026, 3.0% in 2027), before moderating to 2.3% in 2028. Growth is expected to slow to 0.8% by 2028.
